Where we are

Mochi is a 3D ragdoll cat in a cosy study. She now entertains herself, so the app is relaxing to just watch, and care is stress-free: she never gets sick or suffers if you forget her.

What she does on her own

  • A little bird visits about every half minute while she's awake (in every room); she chatters at it and often hops up to the sill for a closer look.
  • Naps on the club chair after kneading the seat; dozes in the sunbeam; plays with her ball by herself.
  • When the bird flies off, she often pats the top book off the sill, looks down at it, then at you ("…it fell.").
  • Something worth watching about every half minute; she curls into a round ball when she sleeps.

Care and saving

  • Saves by itself on the phone; updates never touch anyone's cat. Saves from every earlier version are tested before each release.
  • "Back up or move your kitten" (pencil next to her name) gives a code to restore her on any phone or browser. On iPhone, removing the home-screen app removes its storage, so keep a code.
  • Needs ease down slowly and never fall below 30% from time alone. Naps recharge quickly, for night owls.

Look and sound

  • Her meow is the first version's soft tone (our own, no licence needed); her purr is a free (CC0) recording. No background noise; the fountain is silent.
  • Watch button: the room fills the screen and the controls tuck away.
  • The room (October 9): lightly limed oak floor; a taller window looking out over the dunes to the sea in every room; sunlight across the rug; and a large original abstract over the lamp and chair, palette-knife cobalt, vermilion, black and chalk white, signed in paint "Orion & Chad" in the corner. The Room view frames the furniture closely on any screen.
  • In preview: a limestone fireplace on the right wall with a small log fire (low by day, brighter in the evening) and a mantel with room for Christmas stockings; an olive tree beside the chair; the food and water moved a little away from the hearth. The Room view turns slightly towards the fireplace.
  • ✦ button: room decor. Thanksgiving and Halloween in the Hamptons are available to everyone for now.

Thanksgiving room (from Orion's designs)

  • Oatmeal rug with faded sage stripes and a flax border; flax-linen bed with olive piping and an ivory lining; cream cable-knit throw; linen cushion with sage stripes.
  • Dunes and the sea out of the window (dusky at night).
  • All ten props: ivory and apricot pumpkins, sage gourd, pear bowl, oak branches, oak-leaf garland on the curtain rod, knit throw, linen cushion, brass lantern with a flickering candle, pinecone basket, plus a single oak leaf on the rug.
  • Differences from the drawing: the rug and bed keep the app's existing shapes, and the leaves are a garland on the curtain rod rather than a separate wreath.

Orion's notes (October 8)

  • The lighter rug, olive-trimmed bed and coastal window translate the design well.
  • Asked for subtle woven texture on the rug and bed and a more visible cable knit on the throw, kept light for phones: done, live (small relief textures; the weave and cables catch the light).
  • Confirmed that the Thanksgiving concepts and prop sheet were created for this project and may be used in the commercial app.
  • Asked for the review pack to show Halloween by day and evening, both pumpkins up close and a short felt-bat play clip: done.

How we work

  • Changes go to preview first, with a build number on screen and a review pack; they go live only when Merlin says so.
  • A release is public within a few minutes; the review pack refreshes about 30 to 40 minutes later.
